newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, white metals strong.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, white metals strong.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Thursday as the complex digested Wednesday's big gains, but the strength of silver, platinum and palladium was suggesting the year-long decline in gold may be nearing an end, traders said.

"The shortcovering rally that began yesterday ran into some fresh selling today, but if gold fails to make new lows soon, then it may be time to strap on the seatbelts for a ride back up," said Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta.
COMEX April gold ended down $2.40 at $343.00 an ounce after trading from $346.10 to $342.80, within Wednesday's range. Total estimated volume was 35,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $340.75/25 compared to the London afternoon fix of $342.65 and the New York close Wednesday of $342.80/30.
On Wednesday, gold initially fixed at a new three-year low at $336.90, before a large-scale shortcovering rally by funds led the whole precious metals complex sharply higher.

"The March COMEX gold options expire Friday, Feb 14, which could also account for some of the upward movement in gold prices," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said. "Also, numerous traders may have decided that the bottom of the gold market has been reached, at least in the short run."
The recent extension of the downtrend in gold had been made on falling daily volumes, while momentum indicators also showed the speed of the slide was slowing, analysts noted.

Standard nine and 14-day relative strength indicators (RSI) for gold had been showing some divergence from the price downtrend since early January, but gold remained well below its 21-day (monthly) and 55-day (quarterly) simple moving-average, analysts noted.
Support was still seen around $340.00, while resistance was expected around $348.00 and $350.00.
But it may take more than Wednesday's rally to attract investors back into hard assets while U.S. and European equity markets and the remain strong, analysts warned.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average hit 7,000 Thursday while the dollar remained near its 34-month high against the mark and 48-month high against yen.
Silver remained stronger than gold, with the spot gold/silver ratio sliding to a new 16-month low at 66.41 Thursday.
COMEX March silver ended up 0.7 cent at $5.142 after ranging from $5.180 to $5.105 intraday range, following Wednesday's huge 29-cent gain.

"Rumors that one New York dealer had picked up between five and 50 million ounces of silver over the past few days made the rounds (Wednesday) but there has been no sharp decline in COMEX silver stocks to suggest any such event took place," Kempf said.
COMEX silver stocks fell 206,766 ounces Thursday to 194,499,182 ounces.
Platinum also remained stronger than gold, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread edging higher to $26.50 an ounce after soaring this week from $11.90 last Friday.
NYMEX April platinum ended down $2.20 at $369.50, with NYMEX March palladium $1.00 lower to $140.00.
Palladium prices are now at their highest levels since May 1996 as concerns about Russian supply problems grow, traders said.
